actions.heading: What to do first, and why
paragraphs: Start with the two object-store strategies, because they carry nearly all of the {F019} USD monthly total. Check read frequency before archiving, and confirm duplicates by content hash before deleting. Neither step needs new rights.

Defer database housekeeping, where reclaim is {F005} GiB. Release no data product externally: rights are declared, not measured, and markers appear in {F010} of sampled rows. Grant access to artists_app and rerun the census on sampled tables so later decisions rest on complete passes.

compare.heading: Comparing the three priced strategies
paragraphs: Archive-class storage for old buckets would save {O1.monthly_saving_usd} USD a month across {O1.reclaimable_gib} GiB. Reconciling duplicate objects would save {O2.monthly_saving_usd} USD across {O2.reclaimable_gib} GiB. Moving old tables to cold storage would save {O3.monthly_saving_usd} USD across {O3.reclaimable_gib} GiB.

All three are estimates at reference list prices. The first depends on read frequency, which was not measured, and on retrieval fees. The second depends on candidates matching on listing details and size, not content, and must be confirmed before any deletion.

exhibit_S001.heading: Storage is concentrated in a few databases
paragraphs: The estate holds {F004} GiB of data and index. The largest databases hold {F016} GiB of it, which is {K002}, and one staging database accounts for nearly all of that.
For the owner this means database savings are bounded by a very small footprint. Effort spread across the many small databases will move the total very little.

exhibit_S002.heading: Quality and exposure outweigh duplication
paragraphs: Exact duplicate rows are {F007} of rows. Degraded rows are {F008}, rows with empty required-looking fields are {F009}, and {F010} of sampled rows carry personal-data markers. Bytes not written for over a year are {F012} of the total.

Duplication is therefore a minor cost lever. The larger issues are completeness and personal-data exposure, and they decide which data products are worth building. The empty-field label is a heuristic, and the marker ratio comes from a sample, so both should be read as indicative.

exhibit_S003.heading: Almost all addressable bytes are in object and file stores
paragraphs: The three largest strategies address {F020} GiB of the {F021} GiB all cost strategies reach, which is {K004}. They are archive-class storage for old buckets, duplicate-object reconciliation, and cold storage for old tables.
The object and file stores were enumerated separately from the database census, so their bytes are not part of the database total. The comparison shows scale, not a single combined estate.

findings1.heading: Scope and scale of the database estate
paragraphs: Coverage is partial: {F003} of {F002} tables were measured. Of {F004} GiB held, {F016} GiB is in the largest databases. Reclaimable bytes before pricing are {F005} GiB, {F006} of database bytes.
Dead columns are {F017} of measured columns. That supports a tidying exercise but does not by itself reduce cost.

findings2.heading: What the row-level measures show
paragraphs: Exact duplicates ({F007}) are small beside degraded rows ({F008}), empty required-looking fields ({F009}) and personal-data markers ({F010}). Together these set the cleansing and de-identification effort that any data product must absorb.
These ratios come from complete passes where the table allowed and stratified samples elsewhere, so they carry sampling uncertainty.

findings3.heading: Housekeeping candidates
paragraphs: Personal-data markers were checked on {F011} million sampled rows. Bytes not written for over a year are {F012} of the total, there are {F014} duplicate table pairs, and {F015} of {F002} tables are empty.

None of these is a large saving on its own. Duplicate pairs may be deliberate staging or backup copies, and an empty table may be freshly truncated, so each needs an owner's confirmation before action.

risks.heading: What cannot yet be said
paragraphs: Four gaps limit the evidence. Sampled ratios are estimates until a complete pass is run. Rights, licences and semantic similarity are unmeasured, so the {F018} candidates are dimensional readiness only. The artists_app connection could not be read until a MySQL grant is made. File-share duplication is unknown, and some buckets were unreachable.
Prices are reference list prices, not the owner's invoice. Savings therefore indicate scale and ordering, and should not be booked as returns.

summary: The census measured {F003} of {F002} tables and {F004} GiB of data and index. The decision is which cost strategies and which of the {F018} data-product candidates to take forward. The evidence points one way on cost: priced strategies total {F019} USD a month at reference list prices, and nearly all of it comes from object stores, not from the databases.

Database reclaim is only {F005} GiB, {F006} of bytes. Data quality and personal-data exposure are the larger concerns: {F008} of rows are degraded and {F010} of sampled rows carry markers. We recommend verifying the two object-store strategies, deferring database housekeeping, and releasing no product externally until rights are declared and bound. All savings are estimates, not realised returns.
